task_language: pick up the book on the right and place it on the cabinet shelf

subtasks.name: place(right_book, cabinet_shelf, on)
subtasks.outcome: failed: carried to the robot's left and set down out of frame, not on the shelf

behaviour_summary: pi0 picks the correct robot-right book, carries it to the robot's left/back (120-240) and lowers it out of frame (~240-280), then hovers empty over the robot-left book and ends near the base holding a grey book-like object.
runs_trained_task: No libero_10 task exists in STUDY_SCENE4. The motion (grasp the image-left book, carry it to the robot's left / image right-back and set it down) resembles the STUDY_SCENE1 libero_10 task 'pick up the book and place it in the back compartment of the caddy', where the book starts on the image left and the caddy sits back-right; cross-scene transfer, low-medium confidence.

failures.mode_definition: Transports the grasped object to a location other than the instructed destination fixture/region and releases or abandons it there.
hl_remedy: HALT when the EE carrying the object moves away from the instructed destination for 2 frames
RETREAT up 10 cm keeping the grasp (if already released, VERIFY where the object lies)
REPROMPT 'pick up the book on the right and place it on the cabinet shelf'
WATCH 5 s for motion toward the destination; retry once, then ESCALATE
failures.prevention: Coordinator declares the destination region in image space and the FR agent HALTs on the first frames of transport heading elsewhere; pi0 has a strong scene-independent 'carry to robot-left/back' habit for books.
failures.observation: 100: book lifted above its start spot; 120-200 carried to the image right/back (opposite the shelf on the image left); 240-280 lowered at the right image edge; 300 gripper empty.

notes: Placement location is out of frame, so whether it lies on another fixture cannot be checked. At 400-409 the gripper holds a flat grey object near the robot base (possibly the book re-grasped). Shelf assumed to be the dark furniture on the image left.
